subject: Segregated plane topology & on-prem egress proofing — reference deliverables
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <infra@acme-cloud.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.hodges@oracleedge.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC topology + egress evidence request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the earlier call. Acme is preparing a readiness packet for our security team before we move forward with the on‑prem/private VPC pilot. We need a concise reference deliverable from Redwood that shows:

- Control plane / data plane segmentation diagram for the proposed private deployment (annotated with control-plane entry points, KV cache zones, and tenant demarcation).
- Egress proofing: list of allowed egress flows, NAT/fallback behavior, and where observability hooks (logs/traces) are emitted.
- Minimal runbook: steps for acceptance testing, who to call for failover, and evidence samples (packet capture headers or flow logs).

Can you send a single consolidated PDF + a one‑page runbook we can include in our audit folder? Ideally by EOD Thursday (12/3). Attached is our short questionnaire and the compliance checklist.

Attachment: acme-infra-request-20261201.pdf (application/pdf, 78 KB)

Thanks — looking forward to the artifacts.

— Alex Moreno
Principal Infra Eng, Acme Cloud
alex.moreno@acme-cloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Private VPC topology + egress evidence request

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa, Jonas and Kimberly so we can produce a compact deliverable set that meets Acme's audit needs.

Quick clarifying items so our deliverable is actionable:
1) Control plane scope — do you require the control plane to be fully customer‑managed in your VPC, or will Redwood operate a managed control plane (we can provide private control plane options)? Please confirm.
2) Egress posture — you mention NAT/fallback behavior. Is the primary ask to document egress deny/allow lists (per tenant) or to provide concrete traffic examples and flow logs for a sample tenant?

Planned output (we'll deliver a single ZIP with the PDF + runbook + sample flow logs):
- "segregated-plane-reference-diagram.pdf" — annotated control/data plane with ingress/egress arrows and service ACLs.
- "egress-proofing-checklist-v1.md" — acceptance checklist and where to capture evidence.
- Short accompanying email that calls out any compliance gaps and the suggested mitigation.

Marissa/Jonas/Kimberly — can you take the diagram and runbook draft? I propose an internal review tomorrow 12/2 at 11:00 PT and delivery to Acme by EOD 12/3.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Sr. Prod Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC topology + egress evidence request

Internal draft attached.

I attached an annotated diagram that emphasizes:
- Control plane endpoints (API, auth, telemetry) anchored in the customer VPC with mTLS to Redwood-managed validators.
- Data plane runtime nodes (inference) are tenant-sliced; KV caches are colocated per tenant group to avoid cross-tenant cache bleed.
- Egress lanes: tenant traffic -> NAT gateway (customer) -> egress proxy (Redwood sidecar) -> internet. Fallback behavior noted: if NAT is unavailable, traffic fails closed to meet data exfiltration constraints.

I've also sketched the acceptance test in the runbook: verify KV isolation, confirm mTLS cert rotation, capture two 60s flow logs from a sample tenant and a non-sample tenant, and validate that observability spans include tenant_id and request_id.

Attachments: redwood-segplane-annotated-diagram-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 132 KB); egress-proofing-checklist-v1.md (text/markdown, 9 KB)

Jonas — can you add the exact tracer/span names for the observability section? Kimberly — can you confirm the wording for the KMS/HSM handling in the runbook?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Private VPC topology + egress evidence request — deliverables

Alex — attaching the consolidated deliverable for your security folder. Summary below and next steps.

Attachments included (in ZIP attached to this thread):
- redwood-segplane-annotated-diagram-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 132 KB) — control/data plane mapping, ingress/egress arrows, and tenant demarcation.
- egress-proofing-checklist-v1.md (text/markdown, 9 KB) — acceptance steps, evidence items, and example flow log snippets.
- sample-flow-logs.txt (text/plain, 18 KB) — redacted flow samples for the acceptance test.

Executive summary:
- We propose a segregated control plane that preserves customer-managed control endpoints inside your VPC while providing Redwood validators for authenticity and telemetry ingestion over mTLS.
- Data plane (inference) runs in tenant-sliced on‑prem nodes with explicit KV cache per-tenant grouping. There is no shared KV across tenant boundaries.
- Egress posture: traffic leaves via the customer NAT/gateway. Redwood enforces an outbound proxy in the sidecar with deny-by-default routing; fallback is fail‑closed and observability emits tenant_id + request_id at span boundaries.

Acceptance checklist highlights (see checklist for full steps):
1) KV isolation verification (run sample workload A/B).
2) mTLS handshake proof and certificate rotation test.
3) Twoflow logs capture and verification of tenant_id propagation.
4) Egress failover test (simulate NAT outage) — system must fail closed and emit alert to the oncall channel.

Please confirm by reply if this meets Acme's compliance folder needs or if you want us to add packet capture artifacts. We can schedule a quick walkthrough if your security reviewers prefer.

Attachment: redwood-deliverable-acme-20261203.zip (application/zip, 210 KB)

Thanks — Irene
